text:
Maria: quick ping — I opened a tiny PR to adjust the JS quickstart streaming example and the structured output phrasing. mainly clarifying when/why to explicitly end the stream and adding a short try/catch pattern for safety. low-risk but would love two thumbs.
Sam: can you drop the link?
Maria: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4138 — code changes are minimal, copy tweaks + an extra note about not doing heavy CPU inside the loop to avoid backpressure
Leo: grabbing it now, will scan the iterator example and wording around 'close' semantics
Maria: the critical snippet I want to avoid encouraging is this blocking pattern:
```
const stream = await client.chat.stream({ model: 'rw-stream-1', input });
for await (const pkt of stream) {
  if (pkt.type === 'content') console.log(pkt.text);
}
```
Maria: prefer that we show explicit closure and error handling so users don't leak KV cache or hang sockets
Anne: wording nit — instead of "close the stream" say "cleanly end the stream (await stream.close())" so readers see the explicit call. also mention the close can be awaited for flush.
Sam: code nit: include try/catch/finally, or a for-await with a try inside and finally calling stream.close(). I can paste a tiny example if helpful.
Maria: thanks — I added a try/catch/finally in the PR and a one-line aside about backpressure + not awaiting heavy CPU in the loop. also tightened the structured-output paragraph to avoid implying sync-only handlers.
docs-bot: PR linked to issue #987, automated lint passed ✅
Leo: looks good to me, approve after CI is green. the example is clearer and safer. 👍
Sam: will do a quick render locally and push approve later today if everything looks fine.
Maria: appreciate it — plan to merge once CI is green and no objections within the hour.
_note: Thread contains root message and replies in chronological order. Messages are short, Slack-style.
